widget_description: Running / waiting / total session counts at a glance.
widget_monitor_description: CPU load, memory and session counts from the active datawatch server.
settings_verifier_min_free_mem_mb: Verifier min free memory (MB; unset = 1024, 0 = check off)
settings_verifier_headroom_max_age_hours: Verifier headroom max age (hours; 0 or unset = 24)
settings_quality_gates_enabled: Quality gates enabled (default for all Automata)
settings_gate_scope: Quality gate test scope (full | touched-plus-smoke | touched)
settings_gate_scope_hint: full = the complete test suite. touched = changed packages (and their direct importers). touched-plus-smoke = those plus the smoke test packages below. Empty = the built-in default (full); any runner failure falls back to the full suite.
settings_gate_smoke_packages_hint: Go package patterns that run additionally when the gate scope is touched-plus-smoke, e.g. internal/pipeline, internal/server. Saved as a list.
settings_injection_guard: Prompt injection guard (warn on suspicious Automaton/task specs)
settings_block_on_injection: Block Automaton/task create when injection phrases detected
settings_plan_coverage: Plan coverage check (off | warn | block, default block)
settings_plan_coverage_min_ratio: Plan coverage min ratio (requirement coverage 0-1, default 1.0)
settings_plan_coverage_suppress_created_: Plan coverage: skip files an Automaton plan creates

When on (the default), a file that a task says it creates, or that is new in the plan's own file list inside an existing folder, is not reported as a missing file. A file whose folder cannot be created stays reported.
settings_plan_coverage_scoped_requiremen: Plan coverage: count only scope and constraint sentences
When on (the default), only sentences in the scope and constraint sections of an Automaton spec count as requirements. Single words, file names in a read-first list and quoted phrases do not.
settings_plan_coverage_requirement_secti: Comma-separated section names whose sentences count as requirements (default: scope, constraints). If a spec has none of them, the whole spec is used.
settings_plan_coverage_min_requirement_c: A sentence shorter than this is not counted as a requirement. 0 uses the default (30).
settings_automation_idle_alert_minutes: Automation idle alert (minutes idle before one alert, 0 = off)
settings_automation_triage_alert_minutes: Automaton triage alert (minutes a failed or blocked Automaton may sit before a triage alert, 0 = off, default 30)
settings_automation_create_search_mode: Automaton create search (off, shadow records overlaps without showing them, on shows them, default shadow)
settings_automation_create_search_thresh: Automaton create search threshold (similarity above 0 and at most 1, default 0.5)
settings_host_load_alert_mode: Host load check (off, alert or reap; default alert)
settings_host_load_alert_multiple: Host load alert multiple (a load average above this many times the core count is a breach; default 1.5)
settings_host_load_alert_minutes: Host load alert minutes (how long a breach must last before it warns that Automata may be slowed; default 10)
settings_automation_merge_pending_mode: Automaton merge-pending check (off, shadow or on; default off)
settings_automation_child_inherit: Child Automata inherit from their parent (default on)
settings_automation_child_inherit_help: When on, an Automaton started from another Automaton inherits its parent's project, priority, tags and Automation membership. Values set on the child always win.
prd_new_parent_help: Optional. A child Automaton inherits project, priority and tags from its parent when child inheritance is on.
settings_automation_merge_pending_alert_: Automaton merge-pending alert (minutes a finished Automaton branch may sit unmerged before an alert, 0 = off, default 30)
settings_automation_agent_insert_policy: Automation agent insert policy (allow | require_operator, default allow)
settings_progress_lanes: Progress lanes (parallel lanes of Automata used for utilization, 0 = 5)
settings_progress_inactive_gap_hours: Progress inactive gap (hours without activity that count as an inactive window, 0 = 3)
settings_progress_backlog_path: Progress backlog file (relative paths resolve against the base repository, default docs/plans/README.md)
settings_progress_since: Progress start date (YYYY-MM-DD, empty = first record's creation date)
settings_undeclared_edit_mode: Undeclared edit mode (off | warn | block, default warn)
settings_usage_calculator_variant: Usage calculator layout (pace-gauge | lane-planner | burn-ledger | all)
settings_usage_calculator_safety_points: Usage calculator safety margin (points under the pace line, 0 to 50, default 5)
settings_usage_calculator_cost_per_task_: Usage calculator cost per task (weekly points, above 0, default 0.1)
settings_usage_calculator_baseline_per_2: Usage calculator idle burn (points per 24 hours, 0 to 20, default 3)
settings_usage_calculator_max_lanes: Usage calculator largest lane count (1 to 8, default 3)
settings_usage_calculator_auto_lanes: Auto-lanes: apply the calculator lane advice automatically
settings_usage_calculator_auto_lanes_hin: When on, the daemon adjusts the claude-code inflight cap toward the calculator's pace on its own, never past the operator maximum.
settings_usage_calculator_auto_lanes_spe: Auto-lanes special priority (whole number 0 or above, default 1; 0 counts every open automaton)
settings_usage_calculator_reset_time: Usage calculator reset time (24-hour HH:MM, default 08:00)
settings_usage_calculator_reset_time_hin: Local clock time of the weekly reset, for example 08:00.
settings_usage_calculator_reset_zone: Usage calculator reset time zone (IANA name; empty follows the server's zone)
settings_usage_calculator_reset_zone_hin: An IANA zone name such as America/New_York. Empty uses the zone the daemon runs in, falling back to UTC if that cannot be found. A fixed offset such as +02:00 is not accepted.
settings_usage_calculator_reset_zone_ser: server zone — empty in the config; the reset follows this daemon's local time zone
settings_usage_calculator_keeper: Usage calculator keeper (federation peer that keeps the readings, empty = this daemon)
settings_usage_calculator_keeper_hint: Name of a federation peer. Leave empty to keep the readings on this daemon.
settings_backoff_max_wait_minutes: Usage back-off max wait (minutes when a rate limit has no reset time, default 60)
prd_plan_coverage_warn: Plan coverage below threshold — warning mode
prd_plan_coverage_fail: Plan coverage below threshold — blocked mode
prd_plan_coverage_ack_hint: Note explaining why you acknowledge the failing coverage (required)
prd_plan_coverage_suppressed_title: Suppressed by the plan coverage filters
prd_plan_coverage_filters_help: What the plan coverage filters do
settings_web_search_enabled: Enable web search injection (opencode + goose sessions)
prd_story_llm_hint: Per-story LLM override — empty inherits from the Automaton then the global config. All tasks in this story inherit this unless they have their own override.
prd_settings_write_dirs_label: Writable directories (comma-separated, absolute; empty = project dir)
prd_settings_dirs_hint: Workers may not read or write outside these directories.
prd_scope_warnings_body: The plan references paths outside this Automaton's allowed directories; tasks that do will not start until fixed.
settings_detection_rate_limit_builtin_hi: No list is set, so the built-in per-backend table applies: each backend is matched only on its own throttle line, at the start of the line. Adding a pattern here replaces the table with a plain substring list for all backends.
capacity_pool_host_hint: Machine-wide session limit, shared with interactive sessions — not specific to this Automaton.
capacity_pool_node_hint: Concurrent autonomous sessions this compute node will run at once.
capacity_pool_llm_hint: Concurrent in-flight requests this LLM backend will accept at once.
prd_settings_priority_hint: Used when tasks wait for free capacity.
settings_mcp_resource_subscriptions_help: On: an MCP client can subscribe to the lifecycle events resource (datawatch://events/lifecycle) and get a resource-updated notification when a matching Automata event fires, using the same filter and event kinds as a subscription. Off (default): subscribe is not offered. Needs a daemon restart.
settings_acknowledge_unauthenticated_hel: Silences the startup warning for listeners reachable without authentication; changes no listener.
settings_session_liveness_window_hint: How many seconds without output before a running session counts as stalled. 0 or empty uses the default (120).
settings_session_liveness_overrides_hint: JSON object of backend name to seconds, e.g. {"pi": 300}. 0 turns the idle timeout off for that backend.
settings_session_store_flush_interval: Session store write delay (ms; 0 = write through)
settings_session_store_flush_interval_he: How long the session store waits to batch changes before saving them to disk. 0 saves on every change. Default 1000.
settings_session_store_archive_after_day: Finished sessions untouched for this many days move to the archive file. 0 turns archiving off. Default 14.
settings_session_store_field_cap_kb_help: Largest session text field kept inline in the store. Longer text is cut and the full text goes to a side file. Default 256.
settings_session_store_side_file_cap_kb_: Automaton text longer than this is stored in a side file next to its record. Default 64.
settings_session_summary_terminal_limit: Session summary: ended sessions kept (0 = all)
settings_allowed_project_roots_help: Sessions and test runs may only use a project directory under the autonomous worktree folder (autonomous.worktree_dir), the session workspace root (session.workspace_root, or ~/workspace when unset), or one of these folders. A directory outside every root is refused. Absolute paths only.
settings_git_push_on_complete: Push finished work to the remote
settings_git_secret_scan_mode_help: shadow reports findings without blocking the push; enforce blocks the push when a secret is found; off disables the scan.
settings_git_secret_scan_detectors: Secret scan detectors (comma-separated; empty = all built-in)
settings_git_secret_scan_allow_paths_hel: Files under a matching path are skipped (e.g. vendor, testdata).
settings_git_secret_scan_allow_fingerpri: 16- or 64-char hex fingerprints (sha256 of the secret) of known-good values to allow.
settings_capacity_strict_node_limit: Strict per-node limit (verifier and resumed workers never over-admit a node)
settings_priority_by_kind: Capacity priority by kind (kind=priority pairs; higher runs first; empty = shipped defaults)
settings_priority_by_kind_hint: The kind → priority table (autonomous.priority_by_kind); higher values are admitted first in the capacity queue. Shipped defaults: bug=80, maintenance=70, feature=20, other=0. A priority pinned directly on an Automaton always wins. An empty value clears the table back to the shipped defaults.
settings_defect_intake_automation: Defect intake Automation (Automation name for kind-bug defect filings; empty = off)
settings_defect_intake_automation_hint: The Automation that new kind-bug defect filings flow into (autonomous.defect_intake_automation). Empty by default: each installation chooses its own, and a filing without one is recorded, not filed into any Automation.
settings_capacity_count_pool_by_node: Count each LLM pool by node
settings_capacity_adopt_before_admit: After a restart, admit resumed workers before new work
settings_capacity_fallthrough: Pool fall-through (admit on another idle allowed pool when the requested one is full)
settings_capacity_enabled: Capacity-aware admission (wait for free slots instead of failing)
max_engines_per_node: Max engines per node (1 = one at a time)
settings_max_concurrent_tasks: Max concurrent tasks per Automaton (1 = one at a time)
settings_max_concurrent_tasks_hint: Daemon-wide default. An Automaton's own setting overrides it.
settings_gate_disagreement: When the gate disagrees with a passing verifier
settings_gate_disagreement_hint: warn records both results and lets the task finish; block fails the task on a real regression from a valid baseline. An invalid gate never blocks.
settings_worker_profiles_group_help: Named profiles that size a worker session's context and tools for its job. Built-in profiles are always available.
settings_worker_profile_help: The profile a worker session starts with when no task or Automaton names one. Empty uses the built-in default.
settings_worker_profile_defaults_label: Default profile per role and task kind
settings_worker_profile_defaults_help: The profile each role (planner, worker, verifier, judge) and task kind (implementation, docs, note, final_gate) starts with. Empty keeps the built-in default.
settings_worker_profiles_label: Worker profiles (JSON object keyed by name)
settings_worker_profiles_help: Your named profiles as one JSON object. Built-in names cannot be redefined. Saved when the field loses focus.
settings_worker_profiles_invalid: Worker profiles must be a JSON object keyed by profile name
settings_worker_profile_in_force_help: Read-only. The profile each worker role and task kind starts with, and the tier that set it. Follows the selects above.
prd_gate_invalid_reason: Gate baseline invalid — results are recorded but the gate never blocks
settings_resume_max_age: Resume stale Automata at startup only if active within (sec; 0 = never, -1 = always)
settings_resume_max_age_hint: Applies when the daemon restarts: an Automaton left running is resumed only if its newest activity is within this many seconds. 0 = never auto-resume, -1 = no age limit (missing project directories still prevent a resume). Automata that do not auto-resume are parked as blocked with a reason and raise an operator alert.
settings_archive_grace_minutes: Archive grace for cancelled Automata (min, 0=at once)
settings_inherited_tags_cache_help: How long the shared cache of tags inherited from an Automaton is remembered before it is rebuilt. 0 uses the default (15 seconds); a negative value turns the cache off and rebuilds the index on every read. The docs link opens the Automata tags howto.
settings_capacity_gpu_util: Hold tasks while node GPU is above (% util, 0=off)
capacity_rate_requests_label: Rate ceiling per LLM: requests per window (0 = none)
capacity_rate_requests_help: Most task and verifier starts each LLM may take in one rolling window. 0 = no requests ceiling.
capacity_rate_tokens_label: Rate ceiling per LLM: tokens per window (0 = none)
capacity_rate_tokens_help: Most tokens each LLM may use in one rolling window. 0 = no tokens ceiling.
capacity_rate_window_seconds_help: Rolling window length for the rate ceilings. Only matters when a ceiling is set; 0 uses 3600 seconds.
settings_task_override_statuses: Automaton statuses that accept LLM overrides
settings_snapshot_never_stage: Patterns the snapshot must never stage (comma-separated)
settings_judge_policy: Judge backends (ordered, comma-separated; empty = verifier routing policy)
settings_judge_policy_help: The LLM backends the judges try in order, one attempt each: the Automaton guardrail, plan-review and other autonomous judges. A judge moves to the next backend only when its run hits the time limit. Empty (default) follows the verifier routing policy, so judges use the same modes and backends as verifiers, and the number of attempts equals the number of backends the policy offers.
settings_judge_timeout_help: Time limit for one judge run, counted from when the judge starts. Waiting for a capacity slot does not count. 0 uses the 1800-second (30-minute) default. When a judge times out, the next backend is tried, with a warning each time. After the last backend the Automaton needs review, and an error alert lists every attempt.
settings_judge_size_threshold_help: When the change under review is larger than this many added and deleted lines, the judge tries claude-code first, then the other backends in their usual order. Lines are counted on the Automaton branch against its merge base, with lock files left out. 0 turns this off. The default is 400.
settings_judge_strong_backend_help: Names the strong judge backend a large diff is routed to first when the changed-line count exceeds the judge size threshold. Empty (the default) resolves to the last backend in the judge policy; a value not in the judge policy leaves the policy order unchanged.
settings_judge_verdict_cache_help: Caches a judge's pass or block verdict per (commit sha, judge policy, rules) triple and replays it on later runs instead of running the judge again; a judge that timed out or otherwise did not finish is never cached. Off re-runs the judge every time.
settings_judge_prompt_file_threshold: Judge prompt file threshold (lines, 0=always send in full)
settings_judge_prompt_file_threshold_hel: When the prompt for a judge run is longer than this many lines, it is written to a file and the judge is told to read it, instead of the whole text being typed into the session. 0 always sends the full prompt. Whole number, 0 to 100000.
settings_judge_delivery_wait: Judge extra wait per 1000 prompt lines (sec, 0=none)
settings_judge_delivery_wait_help: Extra time a judge run waits for a long prompt to be delivered, added for every 1000 lines of the prompt. 0 adds no extra wait. Whole number, 0 to 3600.
settings_judge_prompt_file_threshold_err: Enter a whole number of lines from 0 to 100000.
settings_judge_delivery_wait_error: Enter a whole number of seconds from 0 to 3600.
settings_judge_help_link_label: Open the judge settings section of the Automation tab how-to
settings_stuck_running_seconds_help: How long an Automaton may stay running with every task finished and no live session before the watchdog re-checks it once, then blocks it. If only cancelled tasks remain besides completed ones, it advances to the completion review instead. 0 uses the default (900).
settings_pi_thinking_level: Pi thinking level (empty = pi model default; off|minimal|low|medium|high)
settings_verifier_max_run_seconds_help: Total wall-clock limit for one verifier session, counted from when it starts. It is separate from the no-progress timeout above, which only ends a session that shows no activity. 0 turns the cap off. The default is 2700 seconds (45 minutes).
settings_session_start_confirm_help: A session with no assistant output after this long is failed as session never started and retried.
settings_planning_restart_policy_help: What happens to an Automaton that is still planning when the daemon restarts. reattach (default): planning keeps running and the decompose is re-attached to the restarted daemon. restart: planning restarts once after the restart and a decision records it. draft: the Automaton returns to draft, as it does today. Until the restart path reads this setting, every value acts like draft. See docs/howto/restart-with-work-running.md.
compute_field_session_slots: Session slots (0 = derive from GPU data)
websearch_provider_apikey_hint: literal or ${secret:name} — write-only, never shown again
websearch_stats_no_providers: No search providers enabled. Configure one in Settings → Web Search Providers.
rate_limit_no_reset_time: Waiting for the limit to clear

settings_cross_session_enabled: Inject Cross-Session Communication Rule into spawned sessions
settings_vision_describe_timeout_help: How long (in seconds) you give the vision model to describe an attached image. Default is 5 seconds. If the description times out, the image is passed to the session as an @path file reference instead of a description.
prd_task_read_only_hint: This task changes no files, so it may run alongside other tasks without the tree lock.
prd_task_verif_script_hint: A repo-relative script file the Automaton runs to check this task, not a command.

settings_plan_review_mode: Plan review mode — block mode holds approval on a failing verdict
settings_smoke_verification_backend: Smoke verification backend — optional, empty = off. Verifier LLM for smoke / final-gate tasks
prd_plan_review_rerun_tip: Run the configured reviewer on this plan again

settings_plan_tier_hint: Per-tier inflight caps; 0 or blank tier = unlimited. An explicit per-LLM max_inflight > 0 wins.

automation.review.judgeOutcome.next.coul: Nothing to do — it is retried.
automation.review.judgeOutcome.next.time: Nothing to do — it is retried, or see Events.
settings_release_push_and_tag_help: On: the daemon publishes a finished release by pushing it and creating its tag. Off: the release stays local.
settings_release_path_help: How a prepared release reaches the remote. direct_push pushes straight to the branch; pull_request opens a pull request instead. Default direct_push.
settings_release_ci_window_help: Whole minutes the daemon waits for CI on a release before it stops waiting. Must be greater than 0. Default 60.
automaton_release_size_hint: Patch, minor or major adds that step to the version; none adds nothing. Resolve again clears the set size so the layers below decide.
automaton_release_breaking_hint: A breaking change raises its release to the major approval mode, so it is never merged quietly.
automation_milestone_hint: This Automation is a milestone: when it completes it raises the major release step.
settings_attempt_cost_implementation_bac: First attempt backend: implementation tasks (empty = normal choice)
settings_attempt_cost_implementation_mod: First attempt model: implementation tasks (needed for pi, pi-prompt, ollama)
settings_attempt_cost_docs_backend: First attempt backend: docs tasks (empty = normal choice)
settings_attempt_cost_docs_model: First attempt model: docs tasks (needed for pi, pi-prompt, ollama)
settings_attempt_cost_note_backend: First attempt backend: note tasks (empty = normal choice)
settings_attempt_cost_note_model: First attempt model: note tasks (needed for pi, pi-prompt, ollama)
settings_attempt_cost_final_gate_backend: First attempt backend: final gate tasks (empty = normal choice)
settings_attempt_cost_final_gate_model: First attempt model: final gate tasks (needed for pi, pi-prompt, ollama)
settings_attempt_cost_help: Attempt cost: a task's first attempt runs on the cheap worker set here, so the strong worker only starts after the task has failed. Empty keeps the normal choice. Pi, pi-prompt and ollama need a model.
settings_attempt_cost_escalate_after: Failed attempts before the strong worker takes over (0 to 20, default 1)
settings_attempt_cost_resume_limit: Resume context limit for retries, in tokens (0 to 2000000, default 150000; 0 = always start fresh)
settings_attempt_cost_error_refused: The daemon did not save this value. Nothing changed.
settings_attempt_cost_error_network: Could not reach the daemon. Nothing was saved.
settings_attempt_cost_error_range: Enter a whole number from %1$s to %2$s.
settings_daemon_task_modes: Standard task modes (llm, daemon or off, per standard task)
settings_daemon_task_modes_help: Chooses who carries out each decomposition standard task: llm (an LLM session), daemon (the daemon itself, where the template allows it) or off (the template is skipped). daemon is offered only for the templates the daemon can run. final_gate takes only llm or off, and when on it is carried out by the daemon's script gate, not by a model session.
settings_daemon_script_gate_timeout: Script gate time cap (seconds, 0 = no cap, default 900)
settings_daemon_script_gate_timeout_help: The longest one script gate run may take before it is stopped. 0 means no cap. The default is 900 seconds. A negative or fractional value is refused.
settings_daemon_project_gate_command: Project gate command (one line of shell text, empty = unset)
settings_daemon_project_gate_command_hel: The project own build and test command, run by the gate as one line of shell text. Empty leaves it unset. A value with a line break or over 1024 bytes is refused.
settings_daemon_task_number_invalid: Enter a whole number of seconds (0 = no cap)
settings_merge_pipeline_conflict_mode: Merge conflict mode (shadow or on; default shadow)
settings_merge_pipeline_conflict_mode_hi: What a model's conflict proposal that passes the test step does. shadow (the default) records the proposal and applies nothing. on applies the proposal to the merge.
settings_merge_pipeline_conflict_confirm: Merge conflicts to confirm with the operator (a whole number; 0 means none)
The first N conflict resolutions wait for the operator to confirm them. Later resolutions apply without waiting.
automata_empty_std_tasks: No standard tasks yet. Standard tasks are the tasks the decomposer adds to every story. When autonomous.task_templates.enabled is on, the decomposer adds each standard task to every story it decomposes.
settings_decompose_lint_task_templates_h: Configures the standard tasks the decomposer adds to each story.
automata_std_mode_note: Each standard task runs in one of three modes: llm (a model session), daemon (the daemon performs it, no session) or off (not added to the story). The final gate runs through the script gate. The per-task setting is changed in Settings; the setting key is
automata_events_config_in_settings: Automata configuration is in Settings under Automata
automata_events_help_tip: Open the Automata events howto — what each event kind means and how to act on it
automata_events_help_filters: Narrow the event list by kind, project or text. Kind chips toggle on and off.
automata_events_help_card_supervisor_wat: Supervisor watch — what the supervisor is watching right now and why
automata_events_help_card_recent_decisio: Recent decisions — the supervisor’s latest decisions and their reasons
automata_events_help_card_infra_retries: Infrastructure retries — retries caused by infrastructure failures, not by the work itself
automata_events_help_card_automata_check: Automata checks — health checks run against each Automaton
automata_events_help_card_safe_to_delete: Safe to delete — items that can be removed without losing work
automata_events_help_card_cleanup_status: Cleanup status — progress of automatic cleanup after Automata finish
settings_secrets_vault_unreachable_alert: Seconds the Vault backend may stay unreachable before datawatch raises an alert. Default 120; 0 disables the alert.
settings_observer_peer_silent_alert_minu: Raise an alert when a registered observer peer has not pushed for this many minutes. 0 disables the check.
settings.self_config.allow_help: On: an agent holding the self-config group (mcp.allow_self_config) may change its own non-secret settings — config, sessions, observers, LLMs, quota. Off: every self-config attempt is denied and audited.
settings.self_config.audit_denied_help: On (default): denied attempts are logged too, with their reason. Off: only allowed writes are logged.
settings.sensitive_writes.allow_help: On: a model session may run secret, identity and daemon-control tools. Off: each such call is refused and audited. Operator-run calls from the PWA, REST and CLI are unaffected.
settings_usage_entry_intro: Save a usage reading or the extra credit figure here. These are the same forms and the same endpoints as the usage page, so Automata lane advice and the burn guard see the result at once.
settings_usage_entry_saved: Saved. The advice now uses this figure.
settings_usage_entry_help: Usage reading and extra credit help
usage_page_verdict_over: Over budget: at the recent burn you will use about %2$s% of the allowance by the reset (%1$s% used now).
usage_page_verdict_within: Within budget: you have used %1$s% and the burn leads to about %2$s% by the reset.
usage_page_verdict_unknown: No verdict yet: save another reading.
usage_page_empty_body: No readings yet. Save this week's weekly percentage in Settings under Usage reading and extra credit.
usage_page_settings_link: Save a reading or extra credit in Settings
usage_page_allowance_help: How many points of this week's allowance are used, out of the ceiling. The ceiling is 100 plus any extra credit you bought.
usage_page_allowance_next_over: Run fewer lanes or wait for the reset.
usage_page_pace_help: Where your usage stands against the straight line that would use the whole allowance exactly at the reset.
usage_page_pace_state_ahead: %1$s% used, pace line %2$s%: ahead of the line
usage_page_pace_state_behind: %1$s% used, pace line %2$s%: %3$s points of headroom
usage_page_pace_why: %1$s days since the reset, %2$s days left
usage_page_pace_next_ahead: Slow down: you are ahead of the line.
usage_page_burn_help: How many points of the allowance are used each day, with one bar for each day since the reset.
usage_page_burn_next_over: Try %1$s lane(s) to stay inside the allowance.
lane_fill_help_text: One row per lane: its node, its state and what it runs. The bar is full when the lane works, half when it waits on a verifier and empty when idle.
metric_progress_help: Tasks finished out of every task in open work. The trend shows whether the estimated finish date is widening or converging.
metric_cost_help: What the work would cost at API prices. It is not what you pay on a flat plan.
metric_forecast_help: The estimated range of days until open work is done.
unlanded_work_failed: Could not read the unlanded work list: %1$s
unlanded_work_commits: %1$d commit(s) not on the default branch
unlanded_work_delete_confirm: Delete the worktree and branch %1$s? The work is backed up first.
cleanup_skip_reason_live_session: A live session is using the worktree
cleanup_skip_reason_live_lease: A live lease holds the worktree
cleanup_skip_reason_retained: Kept until the retention time ends
cleanup_skip_reason_commits_not_on_base: Has commits not on the base branch
cleanup_skip_reason_no_base_branch: The base branch could not be found
merge_blocked_what: This Automaton has finished work that cannot merge yet, so it is waiting to merge.
merge_blocked_help_link: What does a blocked merge mean? Open the Automaton merge help
sessions_runs_on_tip: The host running the terminal of this session, or its peer name when the session is federated
sessions_model_on_tip: The compute node serving the model of this session, or Anthropic cloud for a Claude session
settings_branch_refresh_enabled: Refresh Automaton branches from main between tasks
settings_branch_refresh_enabled_help: When on, main is merged into an Automaton's branch before each task. A conflict stops the refresh and raises a question.
settings_branch_refresh_behind_limit_hel: A whole number, 0 or more. The refresh runs when the branch is behind main by at least this many commits.
billing_mode_help: api: each call is billed per token. allowance: calls draw on a flat plan allowance. local: runs on your own hardware at no per-call charge. The cost report groups spend by this word.
cost_charts_help_tip: Open the cost report howto — what each chart shows and how to read it
cost_charts_purpose_cost: Tokens, or money in one unit at a time, over time for each group.
cost_charts_purpose_tools: How many tool calls each group made over time. Counts only, never tool names.
cost_charts_purpose_failures: Failed attempts per week by category, and the automatic retries each group used.
cost_charts_purpose_report: One table joining tokens, money, tool calls, failed attempts and retries for each group.
cost_charts_reason_report: %1$s groups, window %2$s, joined from the three charts.
cost_charts_reason_report_partial: %1$s groups, window %2$s. Cost and tool usage are not recorded per Automation, so those columns are blank.
cost_charts_reason_empty_cost: No spend was recorded in this window.
cost_charts_reason_empty_tools: No tool calls were recorded in this window.
cost_charts_reason_empty_failures: No failed, stalled or cancelled attempts in this window.
cost_charts_reason_empty_report: None of the three charts has data for this grouping and window.
cost_charts_reason_not_grouped: This view is not recorded per Automation, only per Project or Automaton.
cost_charts_reason_unavailable: The daemon could not supply this view. %1$s
cost_charts_next_retry: Check that the daemon is running, then press Refresh.
cost_charts_next_showing: Change the grouping or window to look closer.
cost_charts_next_money: Set rates or the monthly price in Settings, or turn USD estimates on.
cost_charts_money_off: Money is not shown: no rate or monthly price is set, or USD estimates are off. Tokens are drawn instead.
cost_charts_tool_names_note: Only counts are recorded, not the names of the tools.
cost_charts_hidden_note: %1$s charts have no data and are not shown. The reasons are in Events.
sessions_search_tip: Matches name, id, backend, tags and state
sessions_filters_tip: Group, saved views and Status, Backend and Tags filters

pending_item_insert_heading: Or insert a pending item (work with no Automaton yet)
compute_observed_peers_hint: These peers report in but have no compute node. Adding one needs an address you enter.
compute_observed_peer_add_tip: Open the add form with this peer name filled in. You type the address; nothing is created until you save.
compute_unanswered_hint: For review only. Nothing here is changed or removed automatically.
projects_manage_confirm_remove: Remove project %1$s? Only the project record is removed. Running sessions and Automaton work are not stopped.

lane_pulse_reason_not_wired: The usage calculator is not wired on this daemon.

dash_card_off_defects_reason: No defects were found or fixed in this window — this card fills as defects are recorded.
dash_series_purpose_lane_util: What it is for: how much of each hour every lane spent holding work, over the last 24 hours.

dash_series_purpose_forecast: What it is for: daily throughput of finished Automata and the range of days to completion.
dash_series_now_forecast: %1$d days of throughput in the window.
dash_series_next_forecast: Next: if the completion range is wide, add capacity or narrow the Automata in progress.
dash_series_purpose_verifier: What it is for: how often each verifier node ran or waited, and how often its runs passed.
dash_series_next_verifier: Next: for a node with many waits or a low pass rate, check that node’s connection and verifier settings.
dash_series_purpose_release_train: What it is for: the tags cut, the CI state and the deploy state of the current release.
dash_series_next_release_train: Next: if CI is failing, open the failing run before cutting the next release.
dash_series_purpose_review_backlog: What it is for: plans and held questions waiting for an operator decision, oldest first.
dash_series_now_review_backlog: %1$d plans and %2$d held questions are waiting.
dash_series_next_review_backlog: Next: answer the oldest held question, or decide the oldest waiting plan.
dash_series_purpose_defects: What it is for: defects found and fixed per day, so you can see whether the backlog is shrinking.
dash_series_now_defects: %1$d found and %2$d fixed in the last 14 days.
dash_series_next_defects: Next: if more are found than fixed, triage the open defects into an Automaton.
dash_card_purpose_console_questions: Questions the Automata are waiting for you to answer.
dash_card_purpose_console_held: Automata that are held or blocked, and why they stopped.
dash_card_purpose_console_lanes: How many lanes are busy, waiting or idle right now.
dash_card_purpose_console_usage: Your plan usage so far, against the pace line.
dash_card_purpose_console_ci_release: Release, ship and repo CI state, with the next action.
dash_card_purpose_integration_status: The latest result from each scheduled job.
dash_card_purpose_tree: Automata with their stories and tasks, as a live tree.
dash_card_purpose_events: A live feed of Automata and session events.
dash_card_purpose_sparklines: Session activity over time, one line per session.
dash_card_purpose_gantt: Automaton tasks over the last 6 hours, as bars.
dash_card_purpose_heatmap: Automata completed and shipped each day this month.
dash_card_purpose_guardrails: Verdicts from the guardrail gates that checked recent work.
dash_card_purpose_ekg: Busy, waiting and idle time for each lane, plus usage burn.
dash_card_purpose_smoke: Progress of the release smoke and end-to-end runs.
dash_card_purpose_memory_scope: How many memories each scope holds.
dash_card_purpose_websearch_usage: Web searches by provider and by who made them.
dash_card_purpose_work_map: Projects, Automations, Automata, tasks and sessions as a graph.
dash_card_purpose_lane_utilization: How much of each lane's time was busy over the window.
dash_card_purpose_lane_utilization_detai: Per-lane busy and idle share, queue wait, backend mix and plan usage over a chosen window.
dash_card_purpose_throughput_forecast: How many Automata should finish soon at the current pace.
dash_card_purpose_verifier_health: How often verifiers pass, fail or have to wait for a node.
dash_card_purpose_release_train: Tags, CI runs and deploys in the window, in order.
dash_card_purpose_review_backlog: Plans and held questions waiting for a decision.
dash_card_purpose_defects_per_day: Defects found and fixed each day.
dash_card_purpose_cost_report: Token spend grouped by Automaton, Automation, backend or week.
dash_card_help_console_questions: Lists the questions Automata have raised and are waiting for you to answer, oldest first. The data is the held-questions list read by the dashboard console. The card is hidden when no question is open.
dash_card_help_console_held: Shows each Automaton that is held or blocked, the reason it stopped and what unblocks it. The data is the held section of the dashboard console. The card is hidden when nothing is held.
dash_card_help_console_lanes: Shows how many lanes are busy, waiting or idle right now, per backend. The data is the lane section of the dashboard console, taken from the capacity ledger. The card is hidden when no lane is configured.
dash_card_help_console_usage: Shows your plan usage so far in points of the weekly allowance, against the pace line for this point in the week. The data is the usage section of the dashboard console, from the readings you enter. The card is hidden until a usage reading exists.
dash_card_help_console_ci_release: Shows the running version, the latest release, the ship policy for push, tag and CI watch, and up to five failing repo CI runs with the next action. The data is the CI and release section of the dashboard console. The card is hidden until a release check or ship policy has been reported.
dash_card_help_integration_status: Shows the latest result of each scheduled job, with when it last ran and whether it passed. The data comes from the schedule results store. The card is hidden when this install has no scheduled jobs.
dash_card_help_tree: Shows each Automaton with its stories and tasks as a live tree, with the status of every node. The data is the Automaton list the dashboard already loads. The card is hidden when there are no Automata.
dash_card_help_orbital: Shows work in progress as a map: projects, Automations, Automata, tasks and sessions, linked by who started what. Click a project to expand it and a session to open it. The data is the work map endpoint. The card is hidden while the map has no nodes.
dash_card_help_events: Shows a live feed of Automata and session events, newest first, such as starts, finishes, blocks and alerts. The data is the Automata event log plus daemon events. The card is hidden until the first event is recorded.
dash_card_help_sparklines: Shows session activity over time as one small line per session, so you can see which sessions are active. The data is the live session list and its activity samples. The card is hidden when no session has activity samples.
dash_card_help_gantt: Shows Automaton tasks that ran in the last 6 hours as bars on a timeline, one row per Automaton, so you can see overlap and gaps. The data is the task start and end times the dashboard loads. The card is hidden when no task ran in that window.
dash_card_help_heatmap: Shows, for each day this month, how many Automata completed and shipped, with release tags marked. The data is the progress history plus the release tags endpoint. The card is hidden when nothing completed or shipped in the last 30 days.
dash_card_help_guardrails: Shows the verdicts of the guardrail gates that checked recent work, with pass and fail counts per gate. The data is the guardrail verdicts in each board's telemetry. The card is hidden until a gate has produced a verdict.
dash_card_help_ekg: Shows the busy, waiting and idle time of each lane over the window, with the usage burn against the pace line. The data is the lane pulse endpoint, from the capacity ledger and your usage readings. The card is hidden until a lane has held or waited on a lease or a usage reading exists.
dash_card_help_smoke: Shows the progress of the release smoke and end-to-end runs recorded on this machine, with pass and fail counts. The data is the smoke run envelopes. The card is hidden when no smoke run has been recorded.
dash_card_help_memory_scope: Shows how many memories each scope holds, so you can see where facts are being kept. The data is the memory statistics endpoint. The card is hidden when the install has no memory entries.
dash_card_help_websearch_usage: Shows web searches by provider and by who made them: session, Automaton, MCP, REST or CLI. The data is the web search statistics endpoint. The card is hidden when web search is off or no provider is configured.
dash_card_help_work_map: Shows projects, Automations, Automata, tasks and sessions as a graph, linked by who started what, with status colours. The data is the work map endpoint. The card is hidden when there are no live sessions or Automaton tasks.
dash_card_help_lane_utilization: Shows how much of each lane's time was busy, hour by hour, over the last 24 hours. The data is the lane utilization series endpoint, from the capacity ledger. The card is hidden when no lane held a lease in that window.
dash_card_help_lane_utilization_detail: Shows each lane's busy and idle share, how long work waited for a lane, the backend mix, the lane fill mode and plan usage in points and tokens, over a window you pick (1 hour, 6 hours, 24 hours or 7 days). A lane flagged idle while eligible work existed names the first waiting item. The data is the lane utilization endpoint, from the Automata ledgers.
dash_card_help_throughput_forecast: Shows throughput per day and how many days the remaining work should take, as a low and high estimate, over the last 30 days. The data is the throughput forecast series endpoint, from saved progress snapshots. The card is hidden until a snapshot has an estimate.
dash_card_help_verifier_health: Shows, per node, how often verifiers passed, failed or had to wait for a slot, with average wait and run times. The data is the verifier health series endpoint. The card is hidden when no verifier ran or waited in the window.
dash_card_help_release_train: Shows release tags, CI runs and the latest deploy in order over the last 14 days, so you can see what shipped and whether CI is green. The data is the release train series endpoint. The card is hidden when the window holds no tag, CI run or deploy.
dash_card_help_review_backlog: Shows the plans and held questions waiting for a decision from you, oldest first, with how long each has waited. The data is the review backlog series endpoint. The card is hidden when nothing is waiting.
dash_card_help_defects_per_day: Shows defects found and fixed each day over the last 14 days, with totals. The data is the defects per day series endpoint, from defect intake records. The card is hidden when no defect was found or fixed in the window.
dash_card_help_cost_report: Shows token spend grouped by Automaton, Automation, backend or week, with input, output, cache and local tokens. The data is the cost report endpoint. The card is hidden when no session with token usage was recorded in the window.
dash_card_purpose_arc_view: One arc as its stages in order, with lanes and plan usage.
dash_card_help_arc_view: Shows one arc (an Automation) as its stages in order, bugs, features and final, each with total, done, running and blocked counts, plus the shared lane usage and the plan usage in points and tokens. A blocked stage names its reason. The data is GET /api/dashboard/arc.
dash_card_purpose_timeline: Every project's Automata as stage bands and member bars.
dash_card_help_timeline: Shows the Automata of every project as an interval chart: each stage a band, each member a bar with its start and end, blocked and waiting time hatched, and today and projected-finish markers. The data is GET /api/autonomous/timeline.
dash_card_purpose_usage_allowance: The weekly usage allowance used so far.
dash_card_help_usage_allowance: Shows how much of the weekly usage allowance has been used, in points, from the usage readings and the usage calculator.
dash_card_purpose_usage_pace: Usage against the pace line for the week.
dash_card_help_usage_pace: Shows the weekly usage level against the pace line, the points a steady pace would have used by now, from the usage calculator.
dash_card_help_usage_burn: Shows the usage points burned on each day of the week, from the usage calculator's daily series.
lane_utilization_help_text: How busy each lane was over the chosen window, how long work waited for a lane, and which lanes sat idle while eligible work existed.
lane_utilization_empty: No lanes were active in this window.
lane_utilization_chart_label: Busy share per lane over time, stacked

plan_records_project_fixed_note: The project is fixed when the record is created.

settings_automata_plan_records_enabled_h: Turns the plan records on or off. Off hides the Records section of the Projects page and answers every plan record route with not found.
settings_automata_plan_records_write_thr: Write plan record changes back to the plans files (off by default)
Meant to mirror record changes back into the plans files. Nothing acts on it yet in this release, so turning it on changes nothing; the files stay a read-only archive. Off by default.
settings_automata_plan_records_import_co: Plan record import conflict policy (suffix, rename or skip, default suffix)
What an import does with a title or row number that is already taken: suffix adds a short suffix and flags the record for review, rename takes a new title from the caller, skip leaves the record out.
settings_housekeeping_repairs_group_hint: Each group is off (does nothing), report (records what it would do) or on (repairs). The default is report.
settings_housekeeping_task_chain_help: What to do when an Automaton's task chain is stuck. off does nothing, report records what would be done, on repairs it.
settings_housekeeping_advance_judge_help: What to do when a judged Automaton did not advance. off does nothing, report records what would be done, on repairs it.
settings_housekeeping_lane_fill_help: What to do when a lane sits idle while work waits. off does nothing, report records what would be done, on repairs it.
settings_housekeeping_leftovers_help: What to do with state left behind by finished Automata work. off does nothing, report records what would be done, on repairs it.
housekeeping_repairs_purpose: Shows each repair group's mode, what it would do and what it did for stuck Automata states.
